Subject: Post-demo: quantifying cost vs latency for pilot

Hi Alex / Sasha —

Thanks again for the demo time this morning. Quick recap and the asks we discussed so we can turn this into a scoped pilot estimate: 

What we heard from you
- Primary product: customer-facing search/chat (interactive). Target peak concurrent users ~50–100.
- Expected token profile: average request 600 tokens in, 1200 tokens out (1.8k tokens/interaction).
- Volume bands you want us to price: small (100k–500k tokens/day), medium (500k–2M/day), large (>2M/day).
- Desired latency SLOs: interactive routes ideally sub-300ms P95; non-interactive/background batch jobs can tolerate up to ~800ms.
- Budget posture: you called out wanting a target unit $/1M tokens to compare across providers — rough ballpark would help us align model/tier proposals.

Our immediate asks from you
1) Can you confirm expected monthly token volume range (pick one band or give a specific estimate)?
2) Do you have strict P95 targets per route (we heard ~300ms interactive, confirm if 250ms would be a hard requirement)?
3) Any procurement constraints (contract length, preferred billing cadence, PO process)?

What we'll deliver next (by EOD Tue)
- A short spreadsheet (attached) with three pricing scenarios per volume band: 1) latency-optimized (streaming + low-latency tier), 2) balanced (multipath routing + batch/stream mix), 3) cost-optimized (batch-friendly, higher latency). Each scenario shows an estimated $/1M-tokens and expected P95 range.
- A one-page note on technical trade-offs (batching settings, streaming overhead, quantization impact).
- Demo recording link attached for your internal review.

Proposed next call: Tue Nov 18, 10:00am PT to walk the spreadsheet and pick a pilot configuration. If that doesn't work, suggest alternatives.

Thanks —

Lauren — thanks for the clear recap and for the recording. A few clarifications from our side so the estimate is useful: 

1) Volume: we're planning a staged rollout. For month 1–3 pilot we expect ~1.2M tokens/day as a peak for the search/chat route (bursty). If the pilot succeeds, steady-state forecast for Q1 is ~3.5M tokens/day.
2) Budget target: for internal benchmarking we want to see numbers around $100–140 per 1M tokens (that range reflects other vendors we've assessed). If you can show delta vs a quantized model variant we can evaluate tradeoffs.
3) Latency: interactive UX requires <=250ms P95 for the primary route; if Redwood's low-latency tier averages 200–250ms we can accept that. Background enrichment jobs can be 500–800ms.
4) Procurement: we have a standard PO path but procurement prefers a 12-month contract (pilot exception allowed) and net-30.

Two optional technical asks: if you can include an estimated cost delta for enabling streaming (server-push) vs pure request/response and a note on prefix/KV caching benefits for our query patterns, that would be very helpful.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — Alex
Alex Romero

Alex / Sasha —

Great context, thank you. A few quick notes inline and next steps from our side: 

- Volume: 1.2M/day pilot, scaling toward 3.5M/day — that maps well to the three-band spreadsheet we'll send. We'll show per-band unit costs and a blended projection for your 3.5M/day profile.

- Budget target: we will produce scenarios that hit the $100–140 /1M token target as a reference. Two important caveats: 
  * Streaming (low-latency) routes carry steady per-token overhead and typically come in higher $/1M than heavily batched throughput.
  * Quantization (8-bit/4-bit) reduces per-token compute cost but can affect latency and sometimes output quality; we'll show a quantized variant in the spreadsheet.

- Latency: we can target <=250ms P95 for interactive with our low-latency tier (single-model streaming + dedicated per-customer pool). We'll include expected P95 ranges per tier in the doc. For background jobs we recommend a cost-optimized batch tier.

- Streaming vs batch: short summary we'll include in the one-pager: 
  * Streaming: best for sub-300ms SLOs on conversational flows, simpler UX, higher unit cost.
  * Batching: reduces per-token cost by aggregating requests; best for asynchronous enrichment or non-real-time inference; introduces tail latency variability.
  * Hybrid/multipath routing: route hot paths to streaming tier and fall back to batch for bulk processing — usually the best cost/latency compromise.

Action items (what we'll do by Tue EOD):
1) Finalized spreadsheet (attached): per-band $/1M estimates for latency-optimized, balanced, cost-optimized.
2) Short technical note with recommended batching settings (batch size, max wait, dynamic batching thresholds), streaming overhead, and quantization guidance.
3) Proposed pilot configuration (2-week dedicated pool + observability hooks) and a PO template for procurement.

Can we confirm Tue Nov 18 10:00am PT for a 30–45 min walk-through? If procurement needs earlier paperwork we can loop legal/procurement on the call or send a PO template in advance.

Thanks —
Lauren
